summary: Lolo NF lookout in Missoula County, MT: 40' L-4 built 1934 (Forest Lookouts says c.1936), last staffed 1955, torn down 1979 after serving as a training site.

facts.status_note: Torn down in 1979 after serving as a lookout training facility; no source describes the site now

events.note: Built 1934 per firelookout.com; Forest Lookouts gives c.1936; the April 1934 order for materials supports the earlier date
Used to train lookouts and smoke chasers (Missoulian, June 21, 1935)
Torn down after serving as a lookout training facility

evidence.quote: This 40' pole L-4 tower, built in 1934

evidence.supports: used as a lookout training facility until torn down in 1979
evidence.quote: training facility until it was torn down in 1979.

evidence.supports: April 1934 order for materials for ten new lookouts, one at Blue Ridge in the Frenchtown district
evidence.quote: One location will be: Frenchtown district--Blue ridge.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts dates the tower c.1936 as a 40-foot pole L-4
June 1935 training of lookouts and smoke chasers at the lookout
evidence.quote: Lookouts and smoke chasers are given training at and from the Blue Ridge lookout.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts marks the site removed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives 1934; Forest Lookouts gives c.1936 citing Kresek. The record uses 1934, which the April 1934 order for materials fits; both dates are shown in the story

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' and design 'L-4' confirmed; design now reads 40' pole L-4. height_m 12.2 is 40 ft converted to metres. Access left out: no source describes access or the site today. Build year conflict (1934 vs c.1936) is the main open question. Forest Lookouts has 'Frenchtown district' and township 17N-23W-31; firelookout.com gives 14 miles east of Superior. No image URLs were in the fetched text (firelookout.com credits the Fire Lookout Museum); none added.
